words.ex: The acolyte helped the priest during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 助手在仪式中帮助了神父。
words.en: An acolyte is someone who assists a priest in certain religious services; more broadly, it can refer to a devoted follower or assistant.

words.tr: adj. 嗜酒的；好饮的；吸水的
words.ex: He is a bibulous man who drinks wine every night.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每晚都喝酒的嗜酒者。
words.en: Bibulous means having a tendency to absorb liquids or being fond of alcoholic beverages.

words.tr: v. 聚合；合并；长到一起
words.ex: The small ponds coalesce into a large lake.
words.ex_cn: 小池塘合并成一个大湖。
words.en: If two or more things coalesce, they come together and form a single group or system.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.tr: n. 煽动者；蛊惑民心的政客
words.ex: The politician is a demagogue who uses angry words to win votes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客是一个煽动者，用愤怒的言辞赢得选票。
words.en: A demagogue is a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular desires and prejudices rather than by using rational argument.

words.ex: The teacher gave an encomium to the student for her perfect score.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生得了满分而给予了赞美。
words.en: A formal expression of praise; a eulogy.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.tr: adj. 勤勉的；勤苦工作的
words.ex: He is sedulous in practicing piano every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天勤奋地练习钢琴。
words.en: If you describe someone as sedulous, you mean that they work hard and pay great attention to detail.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: He dreams of a perfect utopia where everyone is happy.
words.ex_cn: 他梦想一个每个人都很幸福的完美乌托邦。
words.en: An imagined place or state of things in which everything is perfect.

words.tr:
adj. 告别的
n. 告别辞；告别演说
words.ex: He gave a valedictory speech at graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他在毕业典礼上发表了告别演讲。
words.en: A valedictory speech, letter, or performance is one that is intended as a goodbye.

words.ex: The judge will absolve him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法官将免除他所有的罪名。
words.en: If someone is absolved of blame, responsibility, or a sin, they are formally forgiven for it or declared free from it.

words.tr: v. 简述；预示；勾画轮廓
words.ex: He adumbrated the plan in a few words.
words.ex_cn: 他用几句话简述了这个计划。
words.en: To give a faint indication or suggestion of something; to outline or sketch.

words.ex: The teacher often quoted an apothegm to emphasize a point.
words.ex_cn: 老师经常引用一句格言来强调一个观点。
words.en: An apothegm is a short, pithy, and instructive saying or formulation; a maxim.

words.ex: He denied the aspersion on his character.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了对他人格的污蔑。
words.en: An aspersion is a remark or statement that criticizes someone or something and damages their reputation.

words.ex: The bishop appointed a coadjutor to assist with the growing workload.
words.ex_cn: 主教任命了一位助手来协助处理日益增加的工作量。
words.en: A coadjutor is an assistant to a bishop or a person who assists another in a position of responsibility.

words.tr: adj. 先天的；天生的；生性的
words.ex: He was born with a congenital heart problem.
words.ex_cn: 他出生时就有先天性心脏病。
words.en: A congenital disease or condition exists at or from birth.

words.ex: He approached the task with élan.
words.ex_cn: 他以饱满的热情投入这项任务。
words.en: If you do something with élan, you do it with a lot of style and energy.

words.tr: adj. 恰当的；贴切的；关系密切的
words.ex: His comment was germane to the topic.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论与话题恰当相关。
words.en: Something that is germane to a situation or idea is connected with it in an important way.

words.ex: He took a hiatus from work to travel.
words.ex_cn: 他休假去旅行了。
words.en: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, series, or process.

words.tr: v. 监禁；禁闭；把...嵌在墙上
words.ex: He was immured in the old tower for years.
words.ex_cn: 他被囚禁在那座旧塔里多年。
words.en: To confine someone within or as if within walls; imprison.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.tr: adj. 两败俱伤的；内讧的；互相残杀的
words.ex: The two brothers had an internecine fight over money.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟为了钱发生了激烈的内斗。
words.en: If you describe something as internecine, you mean that it involves conflict or struggle within a group or organization.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.tr: adj. 每四年一次的；连续四年的; n. 第四周年纪念
words.ex: The quadrennial event is held to celebrate the founding of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这一每四年一次的活动是为了庆祝城市的建立。
words.en: Happening once every four years.

words.ex: The dentist used an amalgam to fill the cavity.
words.ex_cn: 牙医用汞合金填补了蛀牙。
words.en: An amalgam is a mixture of mercury and another metal, especially one used by dentists to fill holes in teeth. It can also refer to a mixture of different things.

words.tr:
adj. （《圣经》中所说的大洪水前的）古老的；过时的
n.  年迈的人；不合时宜的人
words.ex: He uses an antediluvian typewriter to write letters.
words.ex_cn: 他用一台远古的打字机写信。
words.en: Belonging to the time before the biblical Flood; very old or old-fashioned.

words.ex: The apothecary mixed herbs to help the sick.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师混合草药来帮助病人。
words.en: An apothecary is a person who prepares and sells medicines and drugs.

words.tr:
adj. 苦行的；禁欲主义的
n. 苦行者；禁欲者
words.ex: He lives an ascetic life with no luxury.
words.ex_cn: 他过着简朴的生活，没有任何奢侈。
words.en: An ascetic person has a way of life that is simple and strict, usually because of their religious beliefs.

words.ex: The beneficent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: A beneficent person or organization helps people or results in something good.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.ex: The denizen of the forest knows all the paths.
words.ex_cn: 森林的居民知道所有的路。
words.en: A denizen of a particular place is someone who lives there or is often there.

words.tr: n. 老前辈；老资格；首席
words.ex: He was the doyen of the art world.
words.ex_cn: 他是艺术界的老前辈。
words.en: The doyen of a group or profession is the oldest, most experienced, or most respected person in it.

words.ex: The forest has rich flora with many wild flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有丰富的植物，有许多野花。
words.en: The plants of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.ex: He drank the old man's nostrum for his cough.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了老人的秘方来治咳嗽。
words.en: A nostrum is a medicine, especially one that is not considered effective, that is prepared by someone who is not a doctor.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.tr: n. 博学之士；大文豪；大学者
words.ex: He is a savant who can solve math problems instantly.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位天才，能立即解决数学问题。
words.en: A savant is a person of profound or extensive learning; learned scholar.

words.ex: His work finally received the approbation of his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的工作最终得到了同行的认可。
words.en: Official approval or agreement.

words.tr: adj. 愚昧无知的；落后的；未开发的
words.ex: The village remained benighted and untouched by modern civilization.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄仍然愚昧无知，未受现代文明的影响。
words.en: If you describe people or the place where they live as benighted, you think they are unfortunate or do not know anything.

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: He expatiated on the importance of education.
words.ex_cn: 他详细阐述了教育的重要性。
words.en: To expatiate means to speak or write about something in great detail or at considerable length.

words.tr: n. 攻击传统观念的人；
words.ex: He is an iconoclast who challenges old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑战传统观念的人。
words.en: An iconoclast is someone who criticizes or attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: His laudable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞美的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise and commendation.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.tr: v. 反胃；回吐；依样复述
words.ex: He felt sick and began to regurgitate after eating the spoiled food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了变质的食物后感到恶心，开始反胃。
words.en: To bring up and expel (food) from the stomach to the mouth, as in some birds feeding their young; to repeat (information) without understanding or thought.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.ex: The word 'thou' is archaic in modern English.
words.ex_cn: ‘thou’这个词在现代英语中是过时的。
words.en: Very old or old-fashioned.

words.tr: v. 痛饮狂欢；狂饮作乐
words.ex: They carouse every weekend at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在海滩上狂欢。
words.en: To engage in a noisy, lively drinking party.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.ex: He execrates lies and dishonesty.
words.ex_cn: 他痛恨谎言和不诚实。
words.en: To express great loathing for; to curse or denounce vehemently.

words.ex: He swore fealty to the king.
words.ex_cn: 他向国王宣誓效忠。
words.en: Fealty is a formal and solemn promise of loyalty to a king, queen, or other ruler, especially in the Middle Ages.

words.tr: n. 微观世界；小宇宙；缩影
words.ex: The classroom is a microcosm of society.
words.ex_cn: 教室是社会的一个缩影。
words.en: A microcosm is a small, representative system having analogies to a larger system in constitution, configuration, or development.

words.tr: n. 突然发作；激发；阵发
words.ex: She experienced a paroxysm of coughing during the night.
words.ex_cn: 她在夜里经历了一次剧烈的咳嗽发作。
words.en: A paroxysm is a sudden attack or outburst of a particular emotion or activity.

words.ex: He lost his pecuniary support after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了经济支持。
words.en: Pecuniary means relating to money, especially in terms of financial gain or loss.

words.ex: His rectitude in business dealings was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他在商业交易中的正直是众所周知的。
words.en: Moral integrity; honesty and correctness of judgement or behaviour.

words.ex: The general used a clever stratagem to win the battle.
words.ex_cn: 将军使用了一个巧妙的战略赢得了战斗。
words.en: A stratagem is a plan or scheme, especially one used to outwit an opponent or achieve an end.

words.tr: v. 使无效；使显得愚蠢
words.ex: The boring meeting stultifies his creativity.
words.ex_cn: 这个无聊的会议扼杀了他的创造力。
words.en: To stultify someone or something means to cause them to appear foolish or to be ineffective.

words.ex: He swore a vendetta against his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他向邻居发誓要报仇。
words.en: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel with or campaign against someone.

words.tr: v. 开动（机器等）；驱使；激励
words.ex: The button actuates the machine.
words.ex_cn: 这个按钮启动机器。
words.en: To actuate something means to make it move or operate, especially by means of a mechanism.

words.ex: The water in the swamp is brackish.
words.ex_cn: 沼泽里的水是微咸的。
words.en: Brackish water is slightly salty, as is the mixture of river water and seawater in estuaries.

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.ex: He gave a dolorous look when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他露出悲伤的表情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or appearance as dolorous, you mean that it is very sad and depressing.

words.ex: Malaria is endemic in some parts of Africa.
words.ex_cn: 疟疾在非洲某些地区是地方性的。
words.en: If a disease or condition is endemic in a particular area, it is frequently or regularly found among the people living there.

words.tr: adj. 多产的；肥沃的；丰饶的
words.ex: The fertile land is fecund and grows many crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片肥沃的土地很丰产，能长出许多庄稼。
words.en: Capable of producing an abundance of offspring or new growth; fertile.

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.tr:
adj. 酒醉的；陶醉的
v. 使醉；使陶醉；“inebriate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was inebriated after a night of heavy drinking.
words.ex_cn: 经过一夜的酗酒，他醉了。
words.en: If someone is inebriated, they have drunk too much alcohol and are drunk.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.ex: The bicycle was a precursor to the car.
words.ex_cn: 自行车是汽车的先驱。
words.en: A precursor is something that happened or existed before another thing, especially if it either developed into it or had an influence on it.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.tr: adj. 无定形的；无组织的；
words.ex: The glass is amorphous because it lacks a regular shape.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是无定形的，因为它没有规则的形状。
words.en: Lacking a clear shape or form; not clearly defined or structured.

words.ex: He spoke with animus against his rival.
words.ex_cn: 他带着敌意谈论他的对手。
words.en: A feeling of strong dislike or hatred.

words.ex: The dichotomy between good and evil is common in stories.
words.ex_cn: 善与恶的两分在故事中很常见。
words.en: A dichotomy is a division or contrast between two things that are represented as being entirely different.

words.ex: She was an exemplar of hard work and dedication.
words.ex_cn: 她是勤奋和奉献的典范。
words.en: An exemplar is a person or thing that is considered a very good example of a particular quality or type.

words.tr: adj. 力大无比的；艰巨的
words.ex: The task ahead is herculean, but we are determined to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 前方的任务艰巨无比，但我们决心要成功。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as herculean, you mean that it is extremely difficult and requires a lot of effort.

words.tr: adj. 初始的；早期的；未形成的
words.ex: His idea was still inchoate.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法还很不成熟。
words.en: If something is inchoate, it is just beginning to form or is not fully developed or clear.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.tr: n. 混合物；文学作品的杂集
words.ex: The chef prepared a melange of spices for the dish.
words.ex_cn: 厨师为这道菜准备了一种混合香料。
words.en: A mixture of different elements, especially a collection or medley of various items or types.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.ex: He believes in nihilism and thinks nothing matters.
words.ex_cn: 他相信虚无主义，认为什么都不重要。
words.en: Nihilism is the belief that all values are baseless and that nothing can be known or communicated.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.ex: The rule subsumes all similar cases.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则涵盖所有类似的情况。
words.en: If something is subsumed within a larger group or class, it is included within it, rather than being considered as something separate.

words.tr: adj. 五花八门的； v. “variegate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The garden has variegated flowers in many colors.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有五花八门的彩色花朵。
words.en: Having patches, stripes, or marks of different colors; diversified in appearance.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr: n. 土著；（尤指澳大利亚的）土著居民
words.ex: The aborigine lived in the desert for thousands of years.
words.ex_cn: 这位土著在沙漠中生活了数千年。
words.en: An aborigine is one of the original or earliest known inhabitants of a country or region.

words.ex: The king abrogated the old law.
words.ex_cn: 国王废除了旧法律。
words.en: If someone in a position of authority abrogates something such as a law, agreement, or practice, they put an end to it.

words.ex: The old house came with many appurtenances, including a large garden and a barn.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子附带了许多附属物，包括一个大花园和一个谷仓。
words.en: An appurtenance is a piece of property that is considered to be a part of a larger property and is transferred with it.

words.tr:
n. 露营；野营
v. 野营；临时露营
words.ex: The soldiers set up a bivouac for the night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们为过夜搭建了露营地。
words.en: A bivouac is a temporary camp or shelter, often used by soldiers or mountaineers, that does not use tents or other structures.

words.ex: The cetacean jumped out of the water.
words.ex_cn: 这只鲸类动物跃出了水面。
words.en: A cetacean is a marine mammal of the order Cetacea, which includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises.

words.ex: Many people decry the use of plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 许多人公开反对使用塑料袋。
words.en: If you decry something, you criticize it as being wrong or harmful.

words.ex: The old law fell into desuetude.
words.ex_cn: 这项旧法律逐渐被废弃了。
words.en: The state of being no longer used or practiced.

words.tr: n. 庞然大物；海中怪兽
words.ex: The leviathan moved slowly through the deep ocean.
words.ex_cn: 那只海中怪兽在深海中缓慢移动。
words.en: A leviathan is something that is extremely large and powerful, often used to describe a very large sea creature or a huge organization.

words.tr: adj. 多愁善感的；令人作呕的；自作多情的
words.ex: The movie was too mawkish with its fake tears.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用虚假的眼泪显得过于矫情。
words.en: If you describe something as mawkish, you mean that it is sentimental in a way that you find unpleasant or silly.

words.ex: He misapprehends the simple instructions.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了简单的指示。
words.en: To misunderstand or misinterpret something or someone.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.ex: He purveys fresh bread to the local shop.
words.ex_cn: 他向当地商店供应新鲜面包。
words.en: To purvey means to supply or provide something, especially food, as a business.

words.ex: He had no recourse but to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他别无依靠，只能求助。
words.en: If you have recourse to a particular course of action, you use it when you are in a difficult situation or when you need to achieve something.

words.ex: The table was replete with food.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上摆满了食物。
words.en: If you are replete with something, you have a lot of it and it fills you up.

words.ex: He decided to waive the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他决定放弃这笔费用。
words.en: If you waive a right, claim, or privilege, you do not insist on it or do not use it.

words.ex: His answer was apposite to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题很贴切。
words.en: Something that is apposite is suitable for or appropriate to what is happening or being discussed.

words.ex: He spread calumny about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: A false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

words.ex: He is an expert in the domain of artificial intelligence.
words.ex_cn: 他是人工智能领域的专家。
words.en: A domain is a particular field of thought, activity, or interest, especially one over which someone has control, influence, or rights.

words.ex: The dorsal fin helps the fish swim steadily.
words.ex_cn: 背鳍帮助鱼稳定游动。
words.en: Relating to the back or posterior part of an organism or structure.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.tr: n. 美食家；讲究饮食的人
words.ex: He is an epicure who loves fine food.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱美食的享乐者。
words.en: An epicure is a person who enjoys high-quality food and drink and is very knowledgeable about it.

words.ex: The evidence helps to exculpate him.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据有助于为他开脱。
words.en: To remove blame from someone; to declare or prove someone not guilty of wrongdoing.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.ex: The difference between the two values is infinitesimal.
words.ex_cn: 这两个值之间的差异极微。
words.en: Something that is infinitesimal is extremely small.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.ex: The forest looked primeval and untouched.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林看起来远古而未被破坏。
words.en: relating to the earliest ages of the world or the universe; ancient or prehistoric.

words.ex: She is the quintessence of grace.
words.ex_cn: 她是优雅的典范。
words.en: The quintessence of something is the most perfect or typical example of it.

words.tr:
adj. 锯齿状的；有锯齿的
v. 使成锯齿状；“serrate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The blade of the knife was serrated for cutting bread.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀的刀刃是锯齿状的，适合切面包。
words.en: Having a row of small sharp projections along the edge like a saw.

words.tr: adj. 真实的；确实的；真正的
words.ex: It was a veritable treasure trove of old books.
words.ex_cn: 那是一个真正的旧书宝库。
words.en: You use veritable to emphasize the size, amount, or nature of something.

words.tr: adj. [脊椎] 胎生的；在母体上发芽的
words.ex: The viviparous toad is a unique species that gives birth to live young.
words.ex_cn: 胎生蟾蜍是一种独特的物种，能产下活幼体。
words.en: Giving birth to living young that develop within the mother's body rather than hatching from eggs.

words.ex: He has business acumen and makes smart decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他有商业洞察力，能做出明智的决定。
words.en: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain.

words.tr: n. 鼎盛时期；（人生或事业的)巅峰；册封为神
words.ex: The artist's work reached apotheosis in his final masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家的作品在他的最终杰作中达到了神化。
words.en: The highest point in the development of something; culmination or climax.

words.tr:
adv. 歪地；斜着
adj. 歪斜的
words.ex: The picture was hanging askew on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 那幅画在墙上挂歪了。
words.en: Not in a straight or level position.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.ex: The fence shows the demarcation between the two yards.
words.ex_cn: 这道篱笆标明了两个院子的界限。
words.en: The act or process of marking the limits or boundaries of something.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.ex: She visited her erstwhile home town.
words.ex_cn: 她参观了她从前居住的小镇。
words.en: Former; in the past.

words.tr:
n. 专长；特长
adv. 用强音
words.ex: His forte is playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他的强项是弹钢琴。
words.en: A thing at which someone excels.

words.ex: He was a habitué of the local café, often seen there at the same time every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地咖啡馆的常客，经常在每天的同一时间出现在那里。
words.en: A person who frequents a particular place, especially a place of entertainment.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr: adj. 巡游的；到处走的；兼职的
words.ex: He is a peripatetic teacher who moves from town to town.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位四处奔波的老师，从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: If you have a peripatetic job or way of life, you travel around a lot, living or working in different places for short periods of time.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍的；丰富的；慷慨的；不吝惜的
n. 浪子
words.ex: The prodigal son returned home after years.
words.ex_cn: 那个浪子多年后回到了家。
words.en: A prodigal person spends money or resources in a way that is not careful and is too generous.

words.tr: n. 阿谀奉承的人；谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He is a sycophant who always agrees with his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是附和老板的马屁精。
words.en: A sycophant is someone who praises powerful or rich people in an insincere way in order to get an advantage.

words.tr: adj. 空虚的；茫然的；空洞的
words.ex: His vacuous smile made no sense.
words.ex_cn: 他空洞的微笑毫无意义。
words.en: If you describe someone's mind or smile as vacuous, you are critical of them because they lack intelligence, understanding, or seriousness.

words.ex: The wraith floated silently through the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幽灵静静地飘过那座老房子。
words.en: A wraith is a ghost or ghostlike image of someone, especially one seen shortly before or after their death.

words.ex: The cacophony of car horns made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 汽车喇叭的刺耳噪音让人难以思考。
words.en: A cacophony is a mixture of loud and usually unpleasant sounds.

words.ex: He discussed the project with his confreres.
words.ex_cn: 他与同事们讨论了这个项目。
words.en: A confrere is a fellow member of a profession, fraternity, etc.; a colleague.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.ex: He showed filial love by taking care of his old parents.
words.ex_cn: 他通过照顾年迈的父母表现出子女的孝心。
words.en: Filial is used to describe the relationship between children and their parents, especially emphasizing the duty and respect that children should show towards their parents.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.tr: adj. 无价值的；无效的；无关紧要的
words.ex: The contract was declared nugatory due to a lack of signatures.
words.ex_cn: 由于缺少签名，该合同被宣布为无效。
words.en: If you describe something as nugatory, you mean that it is worthless or has no value.

words.ex: He faced obloquy for speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因说出真相而遭受非议。
words.en: Obloquy is strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: The parity of the numbers is important in this game.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的奇偶性在这个游戏中很重要。
words.en: If there is parity between two things, they are equal to each other.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.ex: He supplicated for mercy.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求宽恕。
words.en: to ask for something in a humble way; to beg earnestly and humbly

words.tr: v. 敷衍；拖延；见风驶舵
words.ex: He decided to temporize until he had more information.
words.ex_cn: 他决定拖延时间，直到获得更多信息。
words.en: To temporize means to delay making a decision or giving a definite answer in order to gain time or avoid committing oneself.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.tr: adj. 快乐安详的；幸福的
words.ex: She had a beatific smile after the prayer.
words.ex_cn: 祈祷后，她脸上带着宁静幸福的微笑。
words.en: A beatific expression, smile, or vision shows great happiness and calmness.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.ex: They had a quiet colloquy after class.
words.ex_cn: 他们课后进行了一次安静的交谈。
words.en: A colloquy is a formal conversation or dialogue.

words.tr: v. 使堕落；使腐化；使败坏
words.ex: The movie might deprave young minds.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影可能会败坏年轻人的心性。
words.en: To make morally bad or evil.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: v. 擦去；忘却；不抛头露面；使（自己）不受人注意
words.ex: He tried to efface the mark with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用橡皮擦掉那个痕迹。
words.en: To efface something means to remove it completely so that it no longer exists or is no longer noticeable.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.tr: n. 地狱；炼狱；无法控制的大火
words.ex: The city was an inferno of fire and destruction.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市成了火与毁灭的地狱。
words.en: An inferno is a place or situation that is extremely hot and fiery, resembling hell.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.tr:
n. 治标药物；缓解剂
adj. 减轻的；缓和的；治标的
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a palliative to reduce his pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种治标药物来减轻他的疼痛。
words.en: A palliative is a drug or medical treatment that relieves suffering without dealing with the cause of the suffering.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；超自然的；难以解释的
words.ex: The psychic claimed to have preternatural abilities.
words.ex_cn: 这位通灵者声称自己拥有超自然的能力。
words.en: Beyond what is normal or natural; supernatural.

words.ex: The experience was a salutary lesson in the importance of preparation.
words.ex_cn: 这次经历是一个关于准备重要性的有益教训。
words.en: A salutary experience or warning is one that has a good effect or influence, especially by showing you the bad results of a particular action or behaviour.

words.ex: The house abuts the park.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子紧邻公园。
words.en: If one thing abuts another, it is next to it or touches it at one end.

words.tr: vt. 恳请，恳求；起誓；（以起誓或诅咒等形式）命令
words.ex: She adjured him to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他讲出真相。
words.en: If you adjure someone to do something, you earnestly request or command them to do it.

words.ex: He can descry a ship on the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 他能看见地平线上的一艘船。
words.en: To catch sight of something or someone that is difficult to see or that is far away.

words.ex: They tried to desecrate the holy church.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图亵渎那座神圣的教堂。
words.en: To desecrate something means to spoil or damage something that is considered to be holy or very important.

words.tr: n. 半吊子；浅薄涉猎者；
words.ex: He is a dilettante who likes painting but never practices.
words.ex_cn: 他是个半吊子，喜欢画画但从不练习。
words.en: A dilettante is someone who studies or does something, but is not serious about it and does not have much knowledge.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.ex: They will exhume the body next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会挖出尸体。
words.en: To exhume a dead body means to dig it up, especially in order to examine it or to find out how the person died.

words.ex: They tried to extirpate the weeds from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图把花园里的杂草彻底清除。
words.en: To destroy or remove something completely, especially a problem or an organization.

words.ex: Her only foible was a tendency to talk too much.
words.ex_cn: 她唯一的缺点就是话太多。
words.en: A foible is a minor weakness or eccentricity in someone's character.

words.tr:
adj. 无力偿付债务的；破产的
n. 破产者；无力偿还者
words.ex: The company went insolvent after years of financial mismanagement.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在多年的财务管理不善后破产了。
words.en: If a person or organization is insolvent, they do not have enough money to pay their debts.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；开玩笑的；闹着玩的
words.ex: He told a jocose joke to make everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个幽默的笑话来让大家笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jocose, you mean that they are playful and humorous.

words.tr: n. 入门；大门；入口网站
words.ex: This book is a portal to learning English.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是学习英语的入门。
words.en: A portal is a large and imposing entrance, doorway, or gate, or a website that provides access or links to other sites.

words.ex: The ancient hunter is the progenitor of our family.
words.ex_cn: 这位古代猎人是我们家族的祖先。
words.en: A progenitor is a direct ancestor of someone or the originator of a particular idea or movement.

words.tr: v. 劝慰；使息怒；谋求好感
words.ex: He brought flowers to propitiate his angry wife.
words.ex_cn: 他带了花去劝慰他生气的妻子。
words.en: To propitiate someone means to make them less angry or hostile by doing something to please them.

words.tr: n. 归还；赔偿；恢复原状
words.ex: The court ordered restitution for the damaged property.
words.ex_cn: 法院命令对受损财产进行赔偿。
words.en: The act of restoring something to its original state or the act of compensating for loss or damage.

words.tr: adj. 酸的； 苦涩的；尖刻的
words.ex: The lemon juice had an acerbic taste.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁有酸味。
words.en: If you say something acerbic, or harshly bitter, you are being sharply critical or sarcastic.

words.ex: The story was a complete canard, spread by those with vested interests.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事完全是一个谣言，是由那些有既得利益的人散布的。
words.en: A canard is a false or baseless story or piece of information, especially one that is deliberately misleading.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.ex: He did not deign to answer her question.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑于回答她的问题。
words.en: If someone deigns to do something, they do it unwillingly and with a feeling of superiority.

words.ex: In his dotage, he forgot his own name.
words.ex_cn: 在他年老糊涂时，他忘记了自己名字。
words.en: Dotage is the period of life in which a person is old and weak, often used to describe a state of being overly fond or foolishly affectionate due to old age.

words.ex: They tried to foist inferior products on unsuspecting customers.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图将劣质产品蒙骗给毫无戒心的顾客。
words.en: If someone foists something on you, they force you to accept it, even though you may not want it.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.ex: The choir sang a paean of praise for the retiring principal.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团为即将退休的校长唱了一首赞歌。
words.en: A paean is a song of praise, joy, or triumph.

words.tr: n. 敏捷的回答；机智的回答
words.ex: The witty repartee between the two comedians kept the audience laughing.
words.ex_cn: 两位喜剧演员之间的机智对话让观众笑声不断。
words.en: A repartee is a quick, witty reply or a conversation full of such replies.

words.tr:
n. 重复部分；再现
v. 重演；重奏
words.ex: The song ended with a short reprise of the chorus.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌以副歌的简短重复部分结束。
words.en: A reprise is a repetition of a piece of music or a performance. It can also refer to the act of repeating something.

words.ex: He has a sartorial style that impresses everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种令人印象深刻的服装风格。
words.en: Sartorial relates to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.

words.tr: adj. 苗条的；体态娇美的
words.ex: He is learning Svelte to build fast websites.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习 Svelte 来构建快速的网站。
words.en: A svelte person is attractively thin and graceful.

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.ex: He works at an apiary near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林附近的一个养蜂场工作。
words.en: A place where bees are kept, especially a collection of hives or colonies of bees kept for their honey.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

words.ex: Smoking exposes you to many carcinogens.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会让你接触到许多致癌物。
words.en: A carcinogen is any substance, radionuclide, or radiation that is an agent directly involved in causing cancer.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr: n. 丰饶的山羊角；聚宝盆；丰饶角
words.ex: The Thanksgiving table had a cornucopia of fruits and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 感恩节的餐桌上摆满了水果和蔬菜的丰饶山羊角。
words.en: A cornucopia is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly represented as a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts.

words.ex: The power will devolve to the local government.
words.ex_cn: 权力将下放给地方政府。
words.en: If you devolve power, authority, or responsibility to a less powerful person or group, or if it devolves upon them, it is transferred to them.

words.ex: The judge made an equitable decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了一个公平的决定。
words.en: Fair and impartial; treating everyone equally.

words.tr: n. 紧急状态；迫切情况（exigency 的复数形式）
words.ex: The company had to adapt quickly to the exigencies of the market.
words.ex_cn: 公司不得不迅速适应市场的紧急情况。
words.en: The exigencies of a situation are the demands or requirements that it creates, especially ones that are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: He believes in fatalism and does not try to change his fate.
words.ex_cn: 他相信宿命论，不愿改变自己的命运。
words.en: Fatalism is the belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

words.ex: The gustatory sense helps us taste food.
words.ex_cn: 味觉帮助我们品尝食物。
words.en: Relating to the sense of taste.

words.tr: n. 细节；细枝末节；琐事；“minutia”的复数
words.ex: The detective focused on the minutiae of the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 侦探专注于犯罪现场的微小细节。
words.en: The small, precise, or trivial details of something.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.ex: The university sent me the prospectus for the course.
words.ex_cn: 大学给我寄了这门课程的简章。
words.en: A prospectus is a formal document that describes a new project, business, or product, especially one that is offered for sale or investment.

words.ex: The vernal equinox marks the beginning of spring.
words.ex_cn: 春分标志着春天的开始。
words.en: Relating to or occurring in spring.

words.ex: The movie shows an apocalyptic future after a big war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影描绘了大战之后预示未来灾难的景象。
words.en: Relating to or predicting the end of the world, especially as described in the Bible.

words.tr: n. 一系列相互关联的事，连结
words.ex: The story was a concatenation of several different tales.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是一系列不同故事的连结。
words.en: The act of linking things together in a series or chain.

words.ex: The nation was convulsed by political scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家因政治丑闻而剧烈震动。
words.en: If someone convulses or if they are convulsed by or with something, their body moves suddenly and violently, often in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.tr:
v. 移居国外；把…逐出国外
n. 侨民；移居国外者
adj. 移居国外的；被逐出国外的
words.ex: He decided to expatriate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他决定移居加拿大以追求更好的生活。
words.en: An expatriate is someone who lives in a country that is not their own, often for work or political reasons.

words.ex: The fetid smell came from the old trash.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自旧垃圾。
words.en: Having an extremely unpleasant smell.

words.ex: The Holocaust killed millions of Jews during World War II.
words.ex_cn: 大屠杀在二战期间杀害了数百万犹太人。
words.en: The Holocaust refers to the genocide of European Jews and others by the Nazis during World War II.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.tr: n. 漫不经心； 漠不关心；无忧无虑
words.ex: He showed insouciance when the teacher scolded him.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评他时，他表现得毫不在意。
words.en: A feeling of not worrying about anything because you do not think anything bad will happen.

words.ex: The boss treated his minion like a servant.
words.ex_cn: 老板把他的手下当仆人对待。
words.en: A minion is a servile follower or subordinate of a powerful person, especially a political leader.

words.tr: adj. 血淋淋的；嗜杀的；残暴的
words.ex: The battle was known for its sanguinary nature.
words.ex_cn: 这场战斗因其血腥的性质而闻名。
words.en: Involving or causing much bloodshed; marked by great slaughter.

words.tr:
adj. 断音的；不连贯的
adv. 断音地；不连贯地
n. 断奏；断续的一段音乐
words.ex: The piano played staccato notes.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴弹奏了断奏的音符。
words.en: In music, staccato is a method of playing notes in a detached, separated manner, as opposed to legato.

words.ex: He lives a sybaritic life with luxury cars and five-star meals.
words.ex_cn: 他过着奢侈的生活，有豪华汽车和五星级酒店的餐食。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sybaritic, you mean that they are fond of luxury and pleasure.

words.ex: He has a thespian talent for acting.
words.ex_cn: 他有戏剧表演的天赋。
words.en: Relating to drama and the theater; an actor or actress.

words.ex: The movie has verisimilitude because it feels real.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影具有逼真性，因为它感觉真实。
words.en: the quality of seeming to be true or real

words.ex: He abnegates his own needs for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他为了家人而放弃自己的需求。
words.en: If you abnegate something, you renounce or reject it.

words.tr:
adj. 辅助的；附属的
n. 后勤人员；附加项目
words.ex: The ancillary staff help the doctors in the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 辅助人员在医院里帮助医生。
words.en: Ancillary means providing necessary support to the primary activities or operation of an organization, system, etc.

words.ex: They exchanged light-hearted badinage during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他们在会议期间轻松地互相打趣。
words.en: Badinage is light, playful, or humorous conversation or writing.

words.tr: v. 把…打扮得俗里俗气
words.ex: She bedizened herself with gaudy jewelry.
words.ex_cn: 她用俗艳的珠宝打扮自己。
words.en: To bedizen means to dress or decorate in a showy or gaudy manner.

words.ex: The project was completed with remarkable celerity.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目以惊人的速度完成了。
words.en: Celerity is the quality of being swift or rapid.

words.tr: n. 注意的焦点； 引人注目的事物；北极星
words.ex: The new museum became the cynosure of all eyes in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这座新博物馆成为全城瞩目的焦点。
words.en: A cynosure is someone or something that is the center of attention or admiration.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.ex: Her lissome movements captivated the audience.
words.ex_cn: 她柔软敏捷的动作吸引了观众。
words.en: If you describe someone as lissome, you mean they are thin, supple, and graceful.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.ex: He is a paragon of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他是诚实的典范。
words.en: A paragon is someone who is considered to be a perfect example of a particular quality.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: He is a staid man who never wears casual clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个古板的人，从不穿休闲服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as staid, you mean that they are serious, dull, and rather old-fashioned.

words.tr: adj. 共栖的；共生的；互惠互利的；
words.ex: The clownfish and the sea anemone have a symbiotic relationship.
words.ex_cn: 小丑鱼和海葵有共栖关系。
words.en: Involving interaction between two different organisms living in close physical association, typically to the advantage of both.

words.ex: As a tyro in the field, he found the learning curve quite steep.
words.ex_cn: 作为这个领域的新手，他发现学习曲线相当陡峭。
words.en: A tyro is someone who is new to and therefore inexperienced at a particular activity.

words.tr: adj. 失败的；夭折的；发育不完全的
words.ex: The abortive plan failed before it started.
words.ex_cn: 这个失败的计划在开始前就失败了。
words.en: Failing to produce the intended result; unsuccessful.

words.tr: v. 非法霸占；僭越；盗用
words.ex: He arrogated the right to make decisions without consulting the team.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自决定，未经团队商议。
words.en: To claim or seize without justification; to assume or appropriate to oneself without right.

words.ex: The medical students studied the anatomy of the cadaver.
words.ex_cn: 医学生们研究了尸体的解剖结构。
words.en: A dead body, especially one that is intended for dissection.

words.ex: The cerebral cortex controls thinking and memory.
words.ex_cn: 大脑皮层控制思考和记忆。
words.en: Relating to the brain or the intellect.

words.ex: He fell into a coma after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后陷入了昏迷。
words.en: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness that lasts for a prolonged or indefinite period, caused especially by severe injury or illness.

words.ex: The two brothers share a strong consanguinity.
words.ex_cn: 这两个兄弟有很强的血缘关系。
words.en: Consanguinity refers to the quality or state of being related to someone by common ancestry or blood relations.

words.tr: n. （东方神话中的）食尸鬼；盗墓者；以做恐怖事情为乐者; n. （Ghoul）人名；（阿拉伯）古勒
words.ex: The ghouls feasted on the remains of the dead.
words.ex_cn: 食尸鬼们享用着死者的残骸。
words.en: A ghoul is an evil spirit or phantom, especially one supposed to rob graves and feed on dead bodies.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.tr: n. 倦怠；疲乏；无精打采
words.ex: He felt lassitude after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后感到乏力。
words.en: A state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy.

words.ex: The stock price hit its nadir last month.
words.ex_cn: 股票价格上个月跌至最低点。
words.en: The nadir of something is the worst or lowest point that it reaches.

words.ex: The nuptials were attended by close family and friends.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼由亲朋好友参加。
words.en: Nuptials refer to a marriage ceremony; a wedding.

words.ex: The onus is on you to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 完成这个项目是你的职责。
words.en: The responsibility for something, especially a duty or task.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.tr: adj. 乐天的；自信的；红润的
words.ex: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the future.
words.ex_cn: 尽管遭遇挫折，他对未来仍然充满希望。
words.en: If you are sanguine about something, you are cheerful and confident that things will happen in the way that you want them to.

words.ex: The appellation 'Doctor' is used to address a person with a medical degree.
words.ex_cn: 称呼 'Doctor' 用于称呼拥有医学学位的人。
words.en: An appellation is a name or title that someone or something is known by.

words.tr: adj. 婚姻的；夫妻（关系）的
words.ex: They live a conjugal life with their children.
words.ex_cn: 他们与孩子一起过着夫妻生活。
words.en: Conjugal means relating to marriage or the relationship between husband and wife.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.ex: The flowers showed efflorescence in spring.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在春天绽放。
words.en: The period or state of flowering or being in bloom; the highest point or stage in a process of development.

words.ex: The effulgence of the sun made the sky bright.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的光辉使天空变得明亮。
words.en: Effulgence is a radiant splendor or brilliance.

words.ex: He wrote an exegesis of the ancient text.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇对古文的阐释。
words.en: Exegesis is the explanation and interpretation of a text, especially a religious one.

words.ex: This movie is a horror genre film.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部恐怖类型影片。
words.en: A genre is a particular type of literature, painting, music, film, or other art form which people consider as a class because it has special characteristics.

words.ex: The artist limned the scene with great detail.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家非常详细地描绘了那个场景。
words.en: To depict or describe in painting or words.

words.ex: The miscreant was caught red-handed.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍被当场抓住。
words.en: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or does not obey the law.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.tr: n. 荒野；[地理]沼泽；系泊（moor 的复数）; v. 使停泊；被系住（moor 的三单形式）
words.ex: The sheep walk on the moors near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在村庄附近的荒原上行走。
words.en: Moors are areas of open, uncultivated land, often covered with heather, that are found in parts of Britain and other countries.

words.ex: His dishonesty became his nemesis.
words.ex_cn: 他的不诚实成了他的天谴。
words.en: Someone's nemesis is a person or thing that is very difficult for them to defeat.

words.ex: He committed a peccadillo by arriving a few minutes late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到几分钟而犯了一个小错误。
words.en: A peccadillo is a small, unimportant fault or sin.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.ex: He is taciturn and rarely speaks.
words.ex_cn: 他沉默寡言，很少说话。
words.en: A taciturn person does not say very much and can seem unfriendly.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: We need to reduce waste in our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

words.ex: He is an equable man who never gets angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个性情恬静的人，从不生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as equable, you mean that they are calm, cheerful, and fair with other people, even in difficult circumstances.

words.ex: Meeting her was pure happenstance.
words.ex_cn: 遇见她纯粹是偶然事件。
words.en: A chance or accidental event; a coincidence.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: n. 骚动；破坏；故意的伤害罪
words.ex: The storm caused mayhem in the city.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在城市中造成了混乱。
words.en: Violent or extreme disorder; chaos.

words.tr:
adj. 危险的；难对付的
adv. 非常地；极度地
words.ex: The situation was parlous, and we had to tread carefully.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常危险，我们必须小心行事。
words.en: A parlous situation is full of danger or uncertainty.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

words.tr: n. 邻近；接近；（血统上的）近亲
words.ex: The propinquity of the two houses made it easy to visit.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子的邻近使拜访变得容易。
words.en: Propinquity refers to the state of being close to someone or something, either in a physical sense or in terms of a relationship.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.ex: The schism divided the church into two groups.
words.ex_cn: 这个分裂使教会分成了两个群体。
words.en: A schism is a division between people, usually belonging to an organization, movement, or religious denomination, due to a difference in opinion or belief.

words.tr:
v. （使）升华；使净化
adj. 升华的；纯化的
words.ex: He tries to sublimate his anger into art.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把愤怒升华成艺术。
words.en: To sublimate means to transform something, especially a strong emotion or desire, into a more positive or acceptable form, often through a process of refinement or elevation.

words.tr: n. 护身符；驱邪物；能产生奇迹的东西；法宝
words.ex: He wears a talisman for good luck.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一个护身符以求好运。
words.en: A talisman is an object which is believed to have magic powers to protect its owner or to bring good luck.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.
